issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java does not provide the expected Farm class and method signatures described in the problem statement. Instead it declares a class named AnimalFarm, contains a duplicated package declaration inside a method, and includes malformed/duplicated content that prevents defining the public class Farm with the required methods (addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong, getters/setters). This structural mismatch between the problem specification (which expects a Farm class with specific methods) and the template will block students from implementing the exercise and from compiling/running code. The solution repository contains a correct Farm class matching the specification, highlighting the template error.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the contents of src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java in the template with a proper public class Farm in package de.tum.cit.ase. The file should not declare AnimalFarm or contain duplicate package declarations. Provide the class skeleton matching the UML/spec: a private List<Animal> animals initialized in a no-arg constructor, public getter and setter for animals, and method stubs with correct signatures for addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), singFarmSong(), and a private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal). Ensure the file compiles so students can implement the bodies as described in the exercise.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a class named 'Farm' (the central aggregate for animals), but the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a class named 'AnimalFarm'. This mismatch between the template class name and the expected 'Farm' identifier will confuse students trying to map the UML/problem description to the provided starter code and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' (and ensure the public class name matches the filename src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java). This aligns the template with the problem statement and the solution, removing the naming mismatch students must reconcile.
